answer.evidence: The transcription opens with "is consciousness, and now Mr. Verschoyle in his final summary", which is the top of the left column on p53. It ends with "acts, including such semi-automatic functions as breathing, into", which is the bottom of the right column. The running head "1932] NEW BOOKS AND OLD 487" also matches.

The transcription begins with "The Spring Spirit in Fiction", the heading at the top of leaf p12. It ends with "HARPER & BROTHERS, Publishers, NEW YORK", the footer at the bottom of that leaf. Its page number 10 matches the folio printed at the top left.

The transcription opens with "34. The personal self seeks to feast on life", which is the bold sutra at the top of p88 under the header PATANJALI'S YOGA SUTRAS. It closes with "as a divine and immortal individuality.", the last line of the body text on p88, and the folio 80 is printed at the foot of the page.

The transcription opens with "of God, as 'that wonder-doer' or the 'crucified wonder-doer Jesus.'" and ends with "which may have read 'contrary to the". Leaf p131 (printed page 115) starts and ends with these exact lines. The 'servants' and 'figure 150' paragraph is in its lower half. Leaf p132 (printed 116) starts with "Law'—κατὰ with the genitive".

The transcription only says "<page-type>blank</page-type>" and has no text. Leaves p103, p104, p105, p106 and p107 are all blank (p107 has only a faint pencil mark in the bottom corner), so it could match any of them. p102 has show-through of a diagram and p108 is a black scan with a tiny line of text at the top.

The transcription starts with 'सर्ग: LVI. निकुम्भबध: पृष्ठ ३११' and ends with 'LXXV. रावणनिर्वाणं ३९७'. These are the first and last entries on leaf p658, whose header reads '६०० सर्गसंग्रहपत्रं'. Leaf p659 is a different page (६०१, cantos LXXVI–XCV).

The transcription describes 'A faint, circular astronomical diagram representing the Sphaera Mundi' and 'A small, faint printer's mark or emblem at the bottom center'. None of the six leaves has these. Pages 103–107 are blank endpaper or board leaves with only foxing and stains; p107 also has a pencil mark in the bottom right. Page 108 is an almost entirely black back scan with only a faint library note at the top. There is no diagram, emblem or Latin text on any leaf, so the transcription describes content that isn't on these pages.

The running head '102 NEW LITERARY TEXTS' and the opening note '9 ἀρῆξαι, ἀρῆξαι. For this explicit, cf. Hom. Il. 1.408' are at the top of leaf p118. The closing note 'Fr. 10 6 σάλπα[. Cf. Archestr. SH 159.1' is at its foot. Leaf p119 is printed page 103 and starts with 'Fr. 11'.

The transcription begins "tire cross, as is generally supposed" and ends "typified regeneration and the life everlasting." Both lines appear on leaf p175, which has the header THE SERPENT AND THE CROSS. and the folio 171. Leaf p176 is folio 172 and starts Chapter IX, The Divine Act.
"PLATE XII" header at top left and caption "PRONAOS OF THE TEMPLE OF HORUS AT EDFU" below the Edfu temple photograph on leaf p80

Heading 'III. The Story of the Champa Raja.', opening 'There was a betel-nut tree near the palace...', and closing 'This is the rea-' all match leaf p230 (folio 208), not p231 (folio 209, which begins 'son that Champa never eats the cow')

Opens with 'e fa' che la detta cassa si commetta o vero si scommetta', which is the first line under the header '140 TRATTATO DELLA PITTURA' on leaf 182. Closes with 'un piè, una gamba, un uc-', which is the last line of that leaf. Leaf 183 is folio 141 and begins 'cello, una bestia'.

The transcription opens with 'auf, du, erhebe dich! Geh einmal vier Schritte', which is the top line of leaf p60. It ends with 'Er zieht aus dessen Brust-', which is the bottom line of that leaf, just above the printed folio 58.

The transcription opens with 'The Mahabharata: An Ethnological Study. By G. J. HELD', which is at the top of the left column on p52 under the header '708 THE ARYAN PATH [November'. It ends with 'one to regulate his conduct in relation', the last line of the right column on that leaf.

The transcription only marks a blank page ('<page-type>blank</page-type>', 'The provided image is a blank page.') and has no text to compare. Pages 101, 103 and 104 are all blank, and page 102 shows only the reverse of page 100 bleeding through. Any of these could be the page it describes.

Opens 'causae concurrunt: tunc eodem die & uerus & noua apparet' at the top of the leaf numbered 41. Heading 'Theorica aspectuum & radiorum' over the zodiac diagram. Ends 'locum astri uerum interceptus iter duos' on the last line above signature F.

The transcription says only '(This page is blank.)' as a blank flyleaf. Leaves p42, p43 and p44 are all blank flyleaves with nothing to tell them apart. It doesn't match p45, which carries a pasted 'BOSTON PUBLIC LIBRARY. CENTRAL LIBRARY. ABBREVIATED REGULATIONS.' slip, or p46, which is a marbled endpaper.

"near Mt. Olympos in Thessalian Dodona" is the opening line under the header '4309. PROSE 69' on p85, and the leaf ends with Fr. 11 note '4 f. If related to Il. 2...'. The leaf for p86 is folio 70 and starts 'people of which went to Troy'.

The transcription is marked 'blank page' with no text. Leaf 316 is the only blank leaf here, with only faint show-through from the other side and no page number. Leaf 317 is not blank: it shows Plate I, papyrus 3431.

Header 'IN ARISTOT. ETHICA'; the text opens with 'desiderio teneretur,hæc quæ nos ex eius ore accepimus' at the top of the leaf and ends with 'declarandam non mediocriter pertinere videntur.' followed by the catchword 'Philo' at the bottom right. The marginal 'fuerunt' in the transcription does not appear on the scan.

The transcription opens with "fore, of 'distributing patronage,' but", the first line of the left column on leaf p63. It ends with "Madras R. NAGA RAJA SARMA", the signature at the bottom of the right column. The running head '[November 1935] CORRESPONDENCE 719' also matches.

The transcription only says 'blank page' and has no text. Page 289 is not blank: it shows Plate VII (papyrus 4041, fr.a and fr.b). Pages 286, 288, 290 and 292 are all blank backs of plates with only faint show-through, so any of them could match.

The transcription opens with "be equally justified in making the same remark about the comic poet", which is the first line of leaf p74, below the header "54 INTRODUCTION". It closes with "It was discovered that the new MS. (A)", the last body line before the footnotes on that leaf. The heading "ix. The Second Book (Musa Paedica, β′)" sits mid-page there, and the footnotes match (1 Vespae 1038, 2 Ach. 1165, 3 Vespae 1194, 4 Eust. 166. 12). Leaf p75 is printed page 55 and opens with "printed by Bekker".

The 'RECIPES. CHAPTER XIII. BAKED BEEF (Cold Meat Cookery)' heading sits at the top of leaf p333. The leaf ends with '(this may be minced if there is not sufficient beef to cut into slices),' at the bottom. No folio is printed on the leaf. Leaf p334 (folio 278) starts mid-recipe with 'well seasoned with pepper and salt...'

The transcription opens with 'home on unavoidable duty following the army' and ends with 'in year 2 it rose still farther.' These are the first and last lines of the leaf printed as page 25. The numbered conclusions 1-8 also match that leaf. The p42 leaf is printed as page 26 and begins 'p. xxiv, paragraph 53'.

The transcription opens with 'las: V. In mente uenit graeculus quidam esuriens' and ends with 'sed prope eam maxima Solis diuersitas colligitur. Nunc cetera'. That matches the first and last lines of p53, under folio 24, and the a–g circle diagram sits at the lower left of that leaf.

The heading 'FIVE LIGHTS AT THE CROSS ROADS / III.—SIMON MAGUS' (the transcription reads 'II.') and the editors' note are at the top of the leaf. The text opens 'Apollonius had at least a biographer' at the top of the left column and ends 'because thou hast thought to obtain this gift of God with' at the bottom of the right column. No folio is printed on this opening page; by sequence it would be 468, since p33 is 467 and p35 is 469.

The transcription opens with "sus, castigauerim, suæq; integritati & ueræ lectioni restituerim", which is the first line at the top of leaf p8. It closes with "Vale, longúmque tibi & amicis uiue.", which is the last line at the bottom of the same leaf. The text continues the dedication to Raimundus Turrianus from p7, where that page breaks off at "elici sen-". Leaf p8 has no printed page number or signature.

The transcription opens with "Volscians, the, Latin tribe, defeated by T. Quinctius, 37" at the top of the left column on p747 and ends with "Zeugma, city of Syria, Crassus crossed the Euphrates at, 211" at the end of the right column. Folio 727 is printed at the bottom right. Leaf p748 is a blank page showing text bleeding through from p747.

The transcription begins "τετάρτην δὲ τὴν Αἰνιανικήν", which is the first line of p462. It ends "ὡς ἐν τοῖς λίθοις ἐγγίνεσθαι", which is the last line of the main text on p462. Footnote 1 ("A river which flows into the Propontis") and the folio number 428 at the bottom of p462 also match.

"Marbled paper cover with a pattern of dark green, red, and yellow swirls". This matches p1, which is the marbled cover with a red leather spine strip on the left edge. P2 has a bookplate, p3 has pencil notes and p4 is a blank leaf.

The transcription's opening line, 'enters into and appropriates more', is the top line of the left column on p33, and its closing words, 'perfection is already realised in an eter-', end the right column. It also includes the running head '1933] CHRISTIAN IMMORTALITY AND HINDU REINCARNATION 105', which is the header of that leaf.

Opens "“I am mourning over the fate of the poor starved soldiers" on the first line under the header "CHING YUH AND KYAIN OO. 83" and ends "the unfortunate parent. Of course, nothing" on the last line of leaf p91. Leaf p92 (folio 84) instead begins "could be done, and again he blamed his son".

The transcription only says 'Blank page' and has no text. Pages 3, 4, 5 and 6 are all blank with no folio numbers, so any of them could match. Page 7 has the title woodcut, page 8 has manuscript notes, and page 9 has printed text with folio 2, so the transcription does not match those.

The transcription says only "blank page", but p7 is the printed table of contents (ОГЛАВЛЕНІЕ). The blank text could match any of the three blank leaves, p4, p6 and p8, so it cannot be tied to one of them.

The transcription's first line, 'In lacke of hem, that ben unware', is the first line of p69, and its last line, 'But if the pouer sheep offende', is the last line of p69. p69 also has the header 'PROLOGUS.', the page number 17 and the signature 'c' at the foot, as the transcription does. The leaf labelled p70 is printed page 18 and opens 'In any thing, though it be lite'.

The transcription only says "The provided image is a blank page." Leaves p3, p4, p5 and p6 are all blank with no text, page number or picture, so any of them fits. p1 is the cover stamped 'SACRO BOSCO. SPHAERA MUNDI. 1501' and p2 has the Boston Public Library bookplate, so neither of those matches.

Heading 'IACOBI FABRI STA-PVLENSIS AD PAV-LVM AEMYLIVM CARMEN.' is at the top of p6. The poem opens 'Quid VIRTVS? quod sol medio clarissimus orbe.' and closes '(Quod breue præcipitur) morum præcepta sequendo.' at the bottom. The leaf has no printed page number or signature, so the transcription's '2' and 'A2' are not on it.

The transcription's first line, '4. When these three, Attention, Contemplation, Meditation, are exercised at once', is the bold sutra at the top of p69 under the 'BOOK III' header. Its last line, 'that they shall see God.', is the final line of p69, just above the folio 61.

The transcription opens with 'translator esto, non conditor antiquorum gestorum', which is the first line of leaf 568 under the header '378 CASSIODORI'. That leaf also has the heading 'XXII. PROVINCIALIBUS HISTRIAE SENATOR PPO.' and ends with 'Praetoria longe lateque lucentia in margaritarum speciem putes esse disposita, ut hinc'. Leaf 569 is printed page 379 and begins with 'appareat, qualia fuerint'.

The transcription begins 'adventure to Hrothgar, and presents to him the hilt of the sword' and ends 'betrothed to the son of Froda^l,'. Those are the first and last body lines of leaf p29, whose header reads 'INTRODUCTION. xxvii'. Footnote k ('The story of Hygd, the queen of Uffi') and footnote l ('Ingeld, the son of Froda') match, as does the signature 'c 2' at the foot. The p30 scan (xxviii) instead begins 'presented the ale-cup'.

The transcription's opening line, 'the moral life more strenuous.', is the top of the left column on p35. Its ending, 'M. A, VENKATA Rao', matches the signature at the bottom right of p35. The running head 'CHRISTIAN IMMORTALITY AND HINDU REINCARNATION' and the folio '107' also match.

The transcription opens with 'augis eius. V. Audiat. C. Quamdiu inquit Sol fuerit in medietate excentrici' and ends with 'Saluus igitur sis amicorum dulcissime. C. Et tu recte ualeto.' Page 65 has the same first line under the printed number 30 and the same last line at the bottom. Page 64 ends with '...ac insuper de motu', which leads into 'augis eius'.

Opens with 'et sacro igni, item strumis cum axungia inveterata' and closes with 'qui parcius insectabantur manicon nominavere, qui nequiter'. Notes 1 'pudoris multi codd.' and 2 'vanas : varias x', and note a on Dioscorides IV. 73, all match leaf p316, which is printed as folio 286.

The transcription describes a 'calibration target with ruler and color checker' ('Oregon Rule Co.', 24 color patches) on a blank page. None of the four leaves matches this. p1 is the October 1890 cover, p2 is the contents page, p3 is 'A POINT ABOUT "LACE."' (folio 1), and p4 is 'THE CENTURY FOR 1890-91.' (folio 2). None of them has a ruler or color checker.

The transcription only says "blank page". Pages 3, 4, 5 and 6 are all blank with no printed text, so it could match any of them. Page 2 has a bookplate, page 7 has the title woodcut and page 8 has show-through and handwritten notes, so those three are ruled out.

The transcription says page-type 'blank' and describes 'A blank, aged page with a uniform tan or light brown color' with 'subtle horizontal striations'. Leaf 54 is the only blank leaf in this run: the back of Plate 4, with plain tan paper and faint streaks. Leaf 55 is actually the opening of Chapter V, 'HISTORY OR STORY?', with printed folio 25, so the stored text belongs to the leaf before it.

The transcription contains no text, only "<page-type>blank</page-type>". Pages 3, 4, 5 and 6 are all blank endpapers or flyleaves with no printed text, so any of them would fit. Page 1 has the cover title, page 2 has the bookplate and page 7 has the title woodcut, so those three are ruled out.

The transcription contains only '<page-type>blank</page-type>' and 'The provided image is a blank page.', with no text to match. Pages 104, 105, 106 and 107 are all blank endpapers or boards. Page 107 has only a faint pencil mark near the bottom right, and page 108 is a black scan-end sheet. Several leaves fit equally well, so the scans can't settle which one this is.

The transcription opens with "but when the Mahatma fasts for", which is the first line of the left column on p31. It ends with "perform the funeral ceremony.", the last line of the right column. Both match the leaf, as do the running head "1934 ] THE MOTHERS OF INDIA'S SAINTS 703" and the footnotes "Maharishi Devandranath Tagore, Autobiography, p. 35" / "Ibid., p. 36" / "Ibid., p. 40".

Opening line 'If Gerbert could be shown to be the translator who wrote this introduction' at top of p750 (printed 704, header 'MAGIC AND EXPERIMENTAL SCIENCE CHAP.'), closing 'Spain to study "astrology" and other arts with the Saracens,' at bottom; side notes 'Question of Gerbert's attitude toward astrology.' and 'His posthumous reputation as a magician.' and footnotes 'III, 43-45' and 'Plurima me docuit Neptanebus ille magister' all match.

The transcription says "The page is blank." with page-type blank. Leaf p654 is the only blank leaf here: it has no printed text, only faint show-through from the facing page. Leaf p655 has the printed contents list 'सर्गसंग्रहपत्रं / युद्धकाण्डं' (sargas I–XV), so the transcription does not match it.

The header '3470. SWORN DECLARATIONS BY PRIESTS 135' and the opening line 'second payment was due before epicrisis' are at the top of leaf p159. The closing lines start the 3471 text, '(m. 3) Ταλ(αὼ) ἱερέ(ων) ... ἀφήλικες υἱοὶ ἰ[ε]ρέων', at the bottom of that leaf. Leaf p160 is printed page 136 and starts with 'καὶ ἱερο[εθ]νῶν προσβάντες'.

The transcription contains no text, only '<page-type>blank</page-type>'. Leaves p101, p103, p104, p105 and p106 are all blank, and p102 shows only faint show-through from p100's diagram and colophon. Only p100 has printed text ('Theorica ultima octauae sphaerae', colophon 'Impressum Venetiis per Io. Baptista Sessa'), and the transcription does not render it. Several leaves match the transcription equally well, so the leaf cannot be identified.

The transcription opens with 'existente in scorpione: qui cum oriatur cum sole' and ends with 'oriuntur in longa uel i breui die artificiali: scilicet et'. Both lines match the first and last lines of leaf p35. That leaf is also printed with folio 15 in the top corner, has the 'De ortu et occasu signorum. Secundum astrologos.' heading, and has two circular diagrams labeled 'Cosmicus heliacus / Cronicus' and 'Equinoctialis / horizon rectus'.

The transcription opens with "Τῶν δ' ἀνθῶν τὰ μὲν ἐκ φλοιοῦ καὶ φλεβὸς" and ends with "ἐν ὑμένι δ' ἔνια τῶν". These match the first and last lines of the Greek text on p112, which has the header THEOPHRASTUS and printed page number 78 at the bottom. The footnotes also match, from 1 "τὰ U; τὸ Ald." to 6 "οὐ conj. Sch.; οὖν Ald.H.". p113 is the English translation of this passage on page 79.

Heading 'RAIMVNDO TVR-RIANO VERONENSI VIRO MAGNANIMO Antonius Francinus S. D.' at the top of page 7. The first text line, 'QVanta mihi cum Io. Baptista Rhammusio', follows the decorated initial Q. The last line, 'quae adeo inuersa erant ut nullus inde uerus posset elici sen=', is at the bottom, above the signature 'a 2'. The leaf has no printed page number.

The transcription begins "Digne pro meritis quam totus non canit orbis" under the header BEATAE VIRGINIS. Leaf p63 has the same opening at the top, the "HYSTORIA NATIVITATIS LAV..." heading in the middle, and "Qui portare suis humeris non distulit agnos" as its last line, above the signature "d iii". Leaf p64 starts differently, with the header HYSTORIA and "In propriis vitae ducens ad gaudia laete".

The transcription's '<page-num>80</page-num>', its opening line '[cαι τους βιους ανα]μι' and its closing heading '4035. AESCHINES De Fals. Leg. 43-45' all match leaf p98 (printed folio 80): the Greek text is at the top, the Roberta Barbis notes are in the middle and the 4035 introduction is at the bottom. The stored page 99 is actually printed folio 81, which has the 4035 text.

The transcription opens with "20 esset. In eo loco qui dominum eius domus salutatum venerant" and ends with "scire, inquam, volo. Atque". These are the first and last lines of the main text on p572, under the header "546 MACROBII". The note "2. quae ratio] sc. sit. Gellius l." closes that leaf's commentary. p573 is printed 547 and begins "ille nihil cunctatus".

The transcription opens with 'On which Iamblichus observes: "The Symbol does not here speak of a woman...' and ends with 'But Iam-', the same as the first and last lines of leaf p313 (folio 287). Leaf p314 is folio 288 and opens with 'blichus' explanation of it is as follows'.

Header '1203. PETITIONS 233'. The text opens 'collection of the debt put into the hands of the ξενικῶν πράκτωρ' at the top of leaf p249, and the Greek text ends at line 25 'μένοντα ἡμεῖν πρὸς τὸν Λεωνίδην τὸν πε-' at the foot of the same leaf. Leaf p250 (printed 234) starts with 'ρὶ πάντων ὧν ἔχομεν'.

The transcription opens with 'महाराज एइ कथा जिज्ञासा करिले आमरा कि उत्तर दिब', which matches the first line of p120 (মহারাজ এই কথা জিজ্ঞাসা করিলে...). It ends with 'मदलेखा कादम्बरीर चरणे पतित हइया आर्तस्वरे कहिल', which matches the last line of p120. Its page number ११२ is the same as the printed folio ১১২ on p120. The transcription is a Devanagari rendering of the Bengali-script printed text.

The transcription only says "This page is blank." and has no text to compare. p4 is a blank paper leaf, but p1 (marbled endpaper) and p3 (only handwritten shelfmarks "A8" and "2000") also have no printed text. A blank-page record therefore cannot pick out one leaf. p2 has bookplates, p5 is the title page, p6 has the Faber Stapulensis poem and p7 has the dedication to Raimundo Turriano.

The opening 'modū Ptolomaeus folet. C. Recte putas' matches the first line under the folio number 25. The closing 'pūctū ei diamettalī' matches the last line above the signature D. The circular diagram labelled a–n is on the right side of the lower half.

The transcription opens with 'On his death his son Chândaghosha becomes Raja' and ends with 'Chândasinha had died, however, without accomplishing his object, and Manikarniká, with'. These are the first and last lines of leaf p29, which has the running head 'INTRODUCTION. 21'. The stored page 30 is folio 22 and begins 'her nurse and attendants'.
